HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Night council on the open deck of the king’s Baekje ship, one oil lamp on a chest between them throwing hard light up into faces. Abe no Hirafu leans in, laughing loudly, slapping the chest, his whole body forward; King Pung leans away from him, polite smile, eyes uneasy. Dark shapes of other captains at the edges, the black river beyond with small lanterns of the moored boats. PLACE (match the attached pl_white_river board and the battle map): the wide grey-brown mouth of the White River, low blue hills on both banks, tidal mudflats, shifting sandbars and reed beds. The Tang fleet of 170 dark tower-ships and warships lies anchored in ONE tight line across the narrow throat of the river, bows to the sea; the Yamato and Baekje boats come in from the open sea to the south-west, hundreds of small open rowing boats packed together. Alongside, a Tang deck stands a man’s height above any Yamato boat; the Tang broadside is a wooden wall the Yamato boats break on. BANNERS BY SIDE: vermilion Tang banners fly ONLY on the dark Tang hulls; red Wa sunburst banners ONLY on the Yamato boats; Tang sails are plain deep red, no emblem; the Tang sun disc holds an abstract black smudge, never a readable character. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = abe, SECOND face = pung. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: ship_baekje (copy its exact shape), ship_yamato (copy its exact shape), place board pl_white_river (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces). ABE NO HIRAFU — Look: Huge bearded seafarer-general: wild black hair in a rough topknot, full black beard, heavy brows, eyes narrowed against wind. Dress: Grey wolf-fur mantle over a long red cape; a blue-grey quilted coat printed with pale leaf patterns, maroon edges and fur-trimmed cuffs; red cord sash. Colour #c8463c. KING PUNGJANG — Look: Prince years: smooth beardless face, soft eyes, black hair in a topknot bound with a red-and-gold cord and a gold pin. Dress: Red robe with black sleeves striped in gold, gold-brocade crossed collar, braided red-and-gold cord sash. Now: King Pungjang (stage portrait): sharper face, a small chin goatee, loose strands falling from the topknot; red king's robe with dark-navy-lined sleeves, gold-scroll shoulders and a long gold cord sash. Colour #e6c76a. PLACE White River (백강 (금강 하구)) — attached board /pl_white_river.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Kingdom banners: copy field colour and emblem from the attached flag_*.png ref onto period silk war-banners — tall poles behind each side, long streamers, small pennants on spear-tips and saddle-backs. Painted silk, wind-whipped, torn and smoke-stained in battle; never a flat modern flag graphic. Each side's banner colour is the clearest colour on its half of the frame, so the kingdom reads at a glance. Wa banners: red silk with a gold many-petalled sunburst. Attached flag /flag_wa.png. Baekje banners: warm yellow silk with a darker gold door-lintel and three gold stars. Attached flag /flag_baekje.png. SHIPS: copy the attached ship board for each kingdom exactly (hull shape, mast count, sail colour and battens) and keep that same ship in every still of the scene. Boards are design only: ignore their bright daylight sky and calm sea, repaint the ship in the scene light. 7th-century timber ships only, never European hulls, cannon or funnels. TRUE SCALE (real 7th-century measures; a man is 1.65 m): ships are drawn life-size against their crews and against each other, never toy boats with giant men. A man standing on deck is about 1/15 the length of a 24 m warship and 1/20 of a 35 m tower-ship; a deck bulwark reaches his chest; the waterline is two men's height below a warship deck. Dozens of men fit along one side of a warship, each one small against the hull, masts four or five men tall. When two kingdoms' ships share a frame, keep their real length ratio. Baekje ship: elegant golden-timber hull with an upswept prow, one large cream battened sail and yellow pennant-sails, yellow Baekje banners. Size: about 18 m long and 4 m wide, about thirty men. Yamato ship: long low white-and-red hull, two masts with pale yellow battened sails, open oared deck. Size: about 15 m long and 3 m wide, gunwale only knee-to-waist high above the water, ten to thirty men rowing standing up; a Tang hull towers over it like a wall. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
